description:

hook.prompt: Cinematic aerial photo, vertical: a fast food restaurant on a busy suburban corner lot at dusk, glowing drive-thru line of cars wrapping around the building, the land parcel and parking lot clearly visible, warm and blue tones, photorealistic, no text, no logos, no brand signage, generic building

mid.prompt: Cinematic photo, vertical: a wrapped burger sitting on top of a stack of property deeds and a ring of building keys on a dark wooden desk, single warm desk lamp, shallow depth of field, photorealistic, no text visible on papers, no logos

scenes.narration: McDonald's sells billions of burgers. But the company itself barely sells any of them.
About 95 percent of McDonald's restaurants are owned and run by franchisees, not the company.
In 2025, customers spent 139 billion dollars at McDonald's restaurants. McDonald's corporate revenue was only 26.9 billion.
So where does McDonald's money come from? Rent. It often owns the land and the building, and franchisees pay rent based on their sales.
In 2025, franchisees paid McDonald's 10.4 billion dollars in rent and 6 billion in royalties.
That's why people call McDonald's a real estate company that happens to sell burgers. Follow for more.
